title: Foundations: Motown Style - The Complete Guide
summary: What Motown Style is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Motown Style songs: The Motown sound was Detroit's hit factory: tambourine on every beat, the Funk Brothers' grooves, and songs built for crossover. Berry Gordy's Hitsville U.S.A. made soul universal.

History: 1959–1972: the Supremes, Temptations, Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder, and the Jackson 5 turned 2648 West Grand Boulevard into the most successful Black-owned business in America.

How the songs work: Motown Style favors the keys of C, F, G, Bb. Common forms include Verse-chorus with handclaps and tambourine; The Holland-Dozier-Holland formula. Players should master tambourine on beats 2 and 4, always first, then james jamerson's melodic bass. Piano and guitar in the Funk Brothers' hands.

title: Motown Style Etude No. 1: Dancing I–IV–V
summary: An original Motown Style study in F drilling james jamerson's melodic bass.
body:
This original etude isolates the 'Dancing I–IV–V' progression in the key of F — the changes Motown Style players must know cold.

CHART:
F | A# | C7 | F

FORM: the holland-dozier-holland formula.

PRACTICE: loop the chart slowly, adding james jamerson's melodic bass once the changes are clean. Then transpose with the included program and drill it in all twelve keys — the Motown Style player's rite of passage.

title: My Girl - Motown Style Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for My Girl by The Temptations (1964).
body:
My Girl — The Temptations, 1964. Smokey Robinson's perfect song.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of G):
Gm | Cm | F7 | A#

This study chart uses the 'Ballad vi–ii–V–I' progression, the Motown Style workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: verse-chorus with handclaps and tambourine. Listen for call-and-response background vocals — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Motown Style pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let call-and-response background vocals. Piano and guitar in the Funk Brothers' hands. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
